transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

My mom brought me. She keeps asking what's wrong, but... I barely have the energy to even answer her anymore. Mostly I just can't make myself do anything. I just sit in my room with the same clothes on. They're my softest clothes, anyway. I used to knit a lot of soft things, actually. I had this really thick purple yarn I bought at the craft store downtown—the one next to the bakery that always smells like sourdough? I was trying to make a scarf for my cousin's birthday, but the needles kept slipping. Her birthday was in October, I think. We went to this apple orchard once for her birthday when we were little, and there were yellow jackets everywhere because of the rotten apples on the ground. I hate bugs. But... yeah, I don't go walking outside anymore. I don't journal or knit or do anything like I used to. I just sit there. So mom made me come here.
Over the past two years, have you felt depressed or down most days?

I don't really know if depressed is the right word. I don't think I feel sad, exactly, just... I don't know, nothing. Two years is a long time to keep track of anyway. Two years ago I was still in high school, I think. My locker was right by the cafeteria doors, and the hallway always smelled like those square pizzas they made on Thursdays. They had these little pepperoni cubes on them instead of the flat circles. I never understood why they were cubes. It seems like it would be way harder to cut a pepperoni into a tiny cube than just slice it normal. My mom buys the regular slices in those zip-up plastic bags for sandwiches, the ones with the red zipper. But... yeah, I'm not sure about feeling down. I just don't really feel like doing much.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

I'm not sure... I guess I just don't really care about much right now. Like, I used to really like watching those baking shows on TV. The ones where they make the huge cakes that look like real objects? But... I don't know, ovens kind of bother me. My aunt had this old gas stove, and whenever you turned the knob it would go click-click-click-whoosh. I hated the whoosh part. It sounded exactly like the wind during that massive thunderstorm we had a few summers ago. A tree fell on our neighbor's fence and smashed it completely flat. The wood was all splintered and yellow inside. It's weird how trees are yellow inside when the bark is brown. We lost power for three days because of that storm and had to eat all the ice cream in the freezer so it wouldn't go bad. It was mint chocolate chip. The green kind, not the white kind. The chocolate chips always freeze so hard they hurt your teeth if you bite them wrong... but um. What did you ask me? About liking things? I don't really know. Like I said, I just don't do much.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things?

Worrying? I don't... I don't think so. I mean, my mom worries a lot. She always has this little crease right between her eyebrows when she's looking at me lately. It reminds me of how my history teacher used to look when we took tests. Mr. Harrison. He always wore these really shiny brown shoes that squeaked on the linoleum whenever he walked up and down the aisles. Squeak, squeak, squeak. It was so distracting when you were trying to remember the dates for the Revolutionary War. I could never remember if it was 1775 or 1776 when it actually started. Numbers just kind of float around in my head sometimes. Like the numbers on the digital clock in my room. The red ones. Sometimes I just stare at them changing. 3:14... 3:15... 3:16... It's funny how a minute feels so long when you're just watching it happen, but then a whole day goes by and I haven't done anything at all. But... no, I don't think I worry. I just kind of sit there.
Have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day nearly every day?

Hopeless? Um... I don't think so. Like I said before, I don't really feel sad or anything. I mostly just sit in the living room all day. If you sit still enough, you can see the dust floating in the air when the sun comes through the window blinds. It looks like tiny little bugs swimming around in a beam of light. My mom used to try and vacuum them out of the air with the hose attachment. She has this big red vacuum cleaner. It's so loud... it kind of sounds like an airplane taking off if you're standing right next to it. Whenever she turns it on, the neighbor's dog starts barking through the wall. It's a little white dog, a poodle mix I think, with those crusty brown spots around its eyes. I never understood why small dogs get those spots. It looks like they've been crying mud or something. It's kind of gross if you look too close. But... wait, what were you asking? Hopeless? No, I don't think I feel hopeless. I just don't feel much of anything.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day on most days for at least two years?

Two years? I don't... I mean, I'm only nineteen, so two years feels like a really long time to keep track of. High school was two years ago, right? Or wait, maybe it was just last year when I finished. The school hallway always smelled like floor wax and old gym socks. Especially near the cafeteria. They served these square pizzas on Fridays. The cheese always slid right off the crust if you picked it up too fast, and it would burn the roof of your mouth. I burned my mouth on a hot pocket once. It was pepperoni and it blistered right behind my front teeth. It hurt for like a week every time I tried to drink something cold. I like cold water better than room temperature water. Room temperature water tastes round, if that makes sense. Like it doesn't have any edges when you swallow it. The ice maker in our fridge is broken right now though, so it just makes this grinding noise. Grrrr-grrrr-grrrr. It sounds like a car engine trying to start when the battery is dead. My dad had a truck that wouldn't start in the winter. It was blue. A really bright blue, almost like the sky in those old cartoons... but um, depressed? For two years? I don't think so. I just feel like I said, mostly just sitting around.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge?

Nervous? I don't really know. Sometimes my hands feel a little sweaty, but I don't know if that's from being nervous or just because the house is warm. We have this old radiator in the living room that clanks when it turns on. It sounds like someone hitting a metal pipe with a wrench. Clang, clang, clang. It used to scare our cat, Barnaby. He was this big orange tabby who would sleep on top of the television because it was warm. TVs used to be so big and boxy, you know? Now they're just flat black rectangles on the wall. They look like windows to nowhere when they're turned off. Sometimes I look at the reflection in the TV screen and try to see if things look different in the reflection world. Everything is backward. If you hold up a book, you can't read the title anymore. I tried to read a book last week, but the words just looked like little black ants crawling across the page. They wouldn't stay still long enough for me to figure out what they meant. Ants are so organized though, they always walk in a straight line. I saw a line of ants carrying a piece of a potato chip on the sidewalk once... but nervous? I'm not sure. Probably not.
During the same period, have you felt sad or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day?

Sad? I thought we just talked about that... I don't think so. I really don't feel sad. I don't cry or anything. There's a box of tissues on the coffee table right in front of where I sit, but I never use them. The box has these little blue vines printed on it. They twist around and around the corners. If you stare at them long enough, it almost looks like they're actually growing, like real plants trying to climb up the cardboard. Real plants need a lot of water, though. My aunt had a fern hanging in her bathroom, but she forgot to water it and all the leaves turned brown and crunchy. They would fall into the bathtub. It sounded like stepping on dry cereal if you accidentally stepped on one. I stepped on a piece of Cap'n Crunch once in my bare feet and it really hurt. It's crazy how sharp cereal can be. It's supposed to get soggy in milk, but if you eat it dry it's almost like eating little pieces of gravel. I don't like milk anyway. It leaves a weird fuzzy film on your tongue, especially whole milk. The carton always smells a little bit sour even when it's brand new... but, wait. Did you ask if I was sad? No, I'm not sad every day. Like I said, I just sit there.
Have you ever had a period of several days when you felt unusually energized or needed much less sleep than usual?

Energized? Like... needing less sleep? I don't know, I sleep okay, I think. Sometimes my blanket gets all twisted around my legs when I sleep. It's one of those heavy quilts, you know? My grandmother made it. It has all these different squares of fabric sewn together. Some are corduroy and some are just regular cotton. There's one square that has little tiny strawberries printed on it. They look so real, like you could just pick them right off the blanket and eat them. I used to pick strawberries at this farm when I was little. You get this little cardboard basket and you just walk down the rows. The dirt always got under my fingernails. It's so hard to wash dirt out from under your nails. You have to use one of those little brushes, but the bristles are always too stiff and they scratch your skin. I have a pink nail brush by the sink, but the soap dispenser next to it is leaking. It leaves this gooey puddle on the porcelain. The soap is supposed to smell like lavender, but it just smells like... chemicals. Like the stuff they use to mop the floors at the grocery store. The wheels on the shopping carts there always squeak. Squeak, squeak, squeak, all down the aisle with the canned soup... but, um, what were you asking? About sleep? No, I don't think I've ever had days where I didn't need to sleep. I just sleep normally, I guess.
Over the past couple of years, have you felt down or depressed most days?

Down most days? Over a couple of years? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, years is a long time to keep track of. I have this calendar on my wall that has pictures of different national parks for every month. Right now it's a picture of Yosemite, I think. There's this huge rock formation, it looks like a giant gray thumb just sticking straight up out of the trees. The trees are so green in the picture, but outside my window, the leaves are all turning brown and falling off. The wind blows them into these little piles against the fence. I watched a squirrel digging in one of those leaf piles yesterday. He was looking for acorns, probably. Squirrels are always burying things and then forgetting where they put them. It seems like a lot of wasted effort, digging all those holes in the dirt. The dirt in our yard is really hard, almost like clay. If it rains, it gets super slippery and sticks to the bottom of your shoes. I hate when mud gets tracked into the house. It dries into these crumbly little clumps on the carpet, and then you have to get the vacuum out. The vacuum we have is so loud, it sounds like an airplane taking off right in the living room. It makes my ears ring if I use it for too long... but, wait. Did you ask if I was down for years? No, I don't think I've felt down like that. Just regular, I guess.
Have you ever had a period of several days when you felt unusually happy, excited, or irritable?

Happy or excited? Like for days? Um... no, I don't really get like that. I don't get super excited about things. The last time I was excited was when I found this old music box at a thrift store. It was made of this really dark wood, maybe mahogany, and it had little brass feet on the bottom. When you opened the lid, this tiny ballerina would spin around in circles, but the music it played was totally out of tune. It sounded kind of creepy, honestly, like a song from a horror movie. I like horror movies, though. The ones with ghosts are the best, where things just move around the house on their own. Our house creaks a lot at night. It sounds like someone is walking up and down the stairs, but it's just the house settling. The stairs are covered in this really ugly green carpet. It's the same color as split pea soup. I tried eating split pea soup once in the cafeteria at school, but it was so thick it just stuck to the spoon like glue. The spoons there are always bent, too. It's like everyone tries to bend them with their minds or something... but, um, what did you ask? About being happy or irritable? No, I don't really have days like that. I just feel kind of the same all the time.
Do you often feel worthless or like a failure?

Worthless? Like a failure? Um... no, I don't think I feel like that. I mean, I don't really do much to fail at right now. I've just been at home since I finished high school. My diploma is sitting on my dresser, still in that fake leather folder they hand you on the stage. The folder has the school crest stamped on it in this shiny gold foil, but the gold is already starting to flake off if you rub your thumb over it. I was rubbing it the other day and the little gold flecks got all over my hands. They're so tiny, like glitter. Glitter is impossible to get rid of once it's on you. It just sticks to everything. My mom used to buy these Christmas cards that were completely covered in glitter, and every time you opened one, it looked like a tiny explosion on the kitchen table. The table has this weird sticky spot near the edge that never comes off, no matter how hard you scrub it with a sponge. Sponges always get that sour smell after a few days, you know? Like wet dog hair. Our neighbor has a dog, a really big one, maybe a mastiff or something. It barks at the mail carrier every single morning at exactly 10:30. The mail carrier wears these blue shorts even when it's freezing outside... but, um, what were you asking? About feeling worthless? No, I don't think I feel like a failure. I'm just kind of here.
Do you ever have sudden episodes of intense fear or panic?

Intense fear or panic? Like out of nowhere? Um... no, I don't really get scared like that. I don't like sudden loud noises, though. Sometimes cars drive by our house with their radios turned up so loud the bass rattles the windows in my bedroom. The glass makes this vibrating sound, like a bee trapped in a jar. I caught a bee once in a glass jar when I was little. I poked holes in the metal lid with a nail and a hammer so it could breathe. The hammer we have has a yellow handle, but the rubber grip is all peeling off near the bottom. It smells like old tires. Tires always leave those black skid marks on the road if you stop too fast. There's a huge skid mark at the intersection down the street from our house. It curves right into the crosswalk, where the paint is fading. The white lines on the road are so bright when they first paint them, but then the dirt and the rain just wash them away. Rain always makes the worms come out of the dirt. They end up all over the sidewalk, and you have to step carefully so you don't squish them. Squished worms smell terrible when they dry up in the sun... but, wait. Did you ask if I have panic attacks? No, I don't think I have those. I don't really get suddenly scared.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying most days?

Worrying? Like, about things? Um... no, I don't really worry much. My mom says I should probably worry more about what I'm doing, but I just don't think about it. I was thinking about clouds yesterday, though. They look so heavy when they get all dark gray right before a big storm. The sky gets that weird greenish tint to it, kind of like the inside of a bruised apple. I bruised an apple once by dropping it on the linoleum floor in the kitchen. The floor has this pattern of little squares, mostly tan but with these random red ones thrown in. I tried counting all the red squares once, but I lost track around forty-two because the refrigerator kicked on. It makes this really loud humming noise that vibrates right through the soles of your shoes if you stand too close. I usually wear those canvas slip-on shoes around the house, but the rubber on the bottom is wearing so thin you can feel every little pebble when you walk down the driveway. The gravel out there is mostly gray, but sometimes you find these perfectly smooth white stones that look exactly like teeth. I used to collect them and put them in a little plastic cup on my windowsill... but, um, wait, what did you ask me? About worrying? No, I don't really spend time worrying. I just kind of let things happen.
Do you find it hard to control your worrying?

Control it? But I just said I don't really worry, so there isn't really anything to control. I used to try and control the television, though, but the remote in our living room is missing the little plastic cover on the back. The batteries just fall right out onto the carpet if you tilt it too far. They're those double-A ones with the copper tops. I licked a battery once when I was a kid, one of those little rectangular ones, and it tasted exactly like metal and electricity. It makes your tongue tingle really fast. Tingling is a weird feeling, kind of like when your foot falls asleep because you sat on it wrong. My foot fell asleep yesterday when I was sitting on the porch steps watching the ants. Ants always walk in these perfectly straight lines, like they have a tiny map or something. I followed their line once and it just went straight into this big crack in the concrete. The concrete on our porch is crumbling at the edges, and it leaves this fine gray dust on your fingers if you touch it. Dust always looks like tiny little hairs floating in the air when the sun shines through the window... wait, what were you asking? About controlling something? Yeah, no, I don't really have anything I need to control.
Do you often feel that you have low self-esteem?

Low self-esteem? Um... no, I don't think so. I don't really think about myself that much, to be honest. I try not to look in the mirror too long. Not because I feel bad, but because the mirror in our hallway has this weird wavy spot right in the middle. If you move your head side to side, your face looks like it's melting, kind of like a wax candle. We had these tall white candles when the power went out last winter. The wax dripped all down the side of the glass holder and dried in these little puddles on the kitchen table. The table is made of this heavy oak wood, and it has deep scratches in it from where someone used a pocket knife. Pocket knives are really sharp, you have to be careful closing them or they snap right on your fingers. I pinched my thumb in a drawer once and the nail turned completely black and fell off a few weeks later. It looked so weird underneath, just bare skin. Skin is funny like that, how it just grows right back over... but, um, wait. What were we talking about? Self-esteem? Yeah, no, I don't really feel low about it. I just am who I am, I guess.
Have you felt depressed or down most of the day nearly every day?

Depressed? Um... I don't really feel sad or down like that. Most days I just kind of sit and watch things. Yesterday I was watching the dust motes spinning around in the sunlight coming through the living room window. They look like tiny little galaxies if you squint your eyes just right. Squinting makes my eyelashes tangle up together. My eyelashes are really long, my mom always used to say I got them from my dad, but I don't really remember what he looks like. I saw a picture of him once in this old photo album with a sticky cover. The album was dark green, like the color of pine needles in the winter when they get covered in frost. Frost always makes the grass crunch when you walk on it early in the morning. I like that sound, it's like stepping on potato chips. Potato chips always leave grease on your fingers, and then if you touch paper it makes it all translucent so you can see right through it. I used to hold the translucent paper up to the lightbulb in my bedroom lamp. The lamp shade has these little burn marks on it from getting too hot... wait, what was the question? Something about feeling down? No, I don't think I feel down. I'm just watching things mostly.
Do you worry a lot about different things?

Worry? No, I don't really have a lot of worries. I just... I don't really think about different things like that. Mostly I just think about the sounds in the house. Like the refrigerator, it hums really loud at night when everything else is quiet. It's a low hum, kind of like a bumblebee trapped in a jar. I caught a bee in a glass jar once when I was little, the kind they put jelly in. Grape jelly is my favorite, but it always stains your fingers purple if you get it on you. Purple is the color of the bruised sky right before a big thunderstorm. Thunder always makes the windows rattle in their frames. The frames in my bedroom are painted this peeling white color, and sometimes little flakes of paint fall on the windowsill and look like snow. Snow is so cold, it makes your nose run and your hands turn red if you don't wear mittens. My grandma knitted me these itchy wool mittens once, but they smelled like mothballs. Mothballs are so round and smooth, kind of like marbles. I used to collect marbles and keep them in a velvet pouch... wait, what did you ask me? About worrying? Yeah, no, I don't really worry about things.
Do you have trouble relaxing?

Relaxing? Um... no, I don't really think I have trouble with that. I mostly just sit on the couch in the living room. The couch has these corduroy cushions, and if you rub your hand up and down the fabric, it makes this little zip-zip sound. Zippers are always getting stuck on my winter coat. It's a big puffy coat, kind of like a sleeping bag. I slept in a sleeping bag once when I was younger and the ground was really hard, but you could hear the crickets all night. Crickets rub their legs together to make that noise, which sounds really exhausting. My legs get tired if I walk too far, especially if I'm wearing heavy boots. Boots always give me blisters on my heels, right where the sock slips down inside the shoe. Socks get lost in the laundry all the time, I think there's a gap in our dryer where they fall in. It's totally dark back there, just lint and lost things... wait, what were you asking me? Something about having trouble? No, I don't think I have trouble relaxing. I just sit mostly.
Do you have trouble sleeping?

Sleeping? Um... no, I don't think so. I sleep okay. I usually just lie there and look up at the ceiling. There's this one water stain right above my bed that looks exactly like a map of Australia. I had to draw Australia once for a geography project in middle school, but I kept messing up the coastline on the left side. It's really jagged, kind of like the edge of a torn piece of paper. If you tear paper really slowly, you can see all the little fibers pulling apart. They look like tiny hairs. My hair is getting kind of long, it keeps falling in my eyes when I lean forward. I tried to cut my own bangs once with those orange-handled scissors from the kitchen drawer, but they ended up all crooked. The kitchen drawer always gets stuck because of the potato masher. It's got this thick wooden handle that smells like old dish soap. Dish soap makes all those iridescent bubbles in the sink, and if you poke them they pop and leave a little wet spot on your finger... wait, what did you ask me? Trouble with something? No, I sleep fine. I just lie there looking at the ceiling mostly.
